assumptions.text: Pins: The gorm.io/gorm, dialector driver and github.com/jinzhu/inflection versions in the module's go.mod are the ones that built the binary that migrated the database (pins: {"gorm.io/gorm": "<v>", "gorm.io/driver/<d>": "<v>", ...}), and gorm's DDL code is the same as at the verified pins for every version in the accepted range (O5: verified at 1.25.12 and 1.31.2; a newer v1 version is read under this assumption, shown as "rules verified at gorm 1.25.12-1.31.2"); a dialector driver pin outside the verified driver versions (postgres v1.5.11 and v1.6.3, sqlite v1.5.7 and v1.6.0, glebarez sqlite v1.11.0, mysql v1.6.0) is read under it too and shown with the verified versions.

Schema deployed: The database was created by the migrate calls read, on an empty database, and every call succeeded (the application started), and no other code changed the schema: a read Migrator() DDL call or Exec/Raw with DDL text is marked (the tables it may change keep partial sets, the table list may be incomplete), while SQL the application builds at run time or a separate migration tool runs is outside the records. AutoMigrate on existing tables only adds columns, indexes and constraints; a database created by older versions of the application (gotify has kept one since 2018) can hold more.
Dialect: The database is of the group's dialect: the single dialector every read gorm.Open site uses, or one of several chosen at runtime (then the dialect-dependent facts are claimed per dialect).
No runtime naming changes: No code changes the naming strategy, inflection's rules or the configuration after gorm.Open beyond what is read (a read mutation makes the dependent facts unknown).

Schema parse order: No code parses a model's schema (a query, db.Model(...), another goroutine) before the migrate calls that the order rule reads, so GORM's schema cache holds what the migrate calls put there.
Build: The packages compile as read: no build constraint, generated file or vendor copy changes the struct set or the migrate calls.

initialize.instructions: Graphvein answers questions about this codebase from a stored index: routes and their handlers, the callers of a route or function, what a change or a node reaches, tables and the code that reads or writes them, and unresolved calls. Every answer carries the index freshness, its labels, unknowns, assumptions and the caps that bound it (an empty result with a bound cap means unknown beyond the cap, not none). Absence of a result is never proof of absence. For such questions about this repository, search for and use Graphvein's tools before reading files.

tools.description: Who calls this function or route? Stored call paths up to depth (default 1, a route 2; at most 10), with provenance and confidence = weakest edge, the caps that bound, '? not modelled' ends and, for a route, near misses. An empty result with a bound cap means unknown beyond the cap, not none.

depth.description: steps to walk (callers default 1, a route 2; impact default 3; at most 10)

repository.description: project mode: the member whose nodes the target is looked up in

scope.description: production (default: results in test code left out and counted) or all

target.description: node identity, 'METHOD /path' as served (the route), a name or a qualified-name suffix at a name boundary

unknowns_cursor.description: the next_cursor of an unknown's list

unknowns_limit.description: items of each list an unknown carries (call sites, sites, stubs; default 20, at most 500)

tools.title: Callers

tools.description: The full path from UI code and client calls through routes and handlers to tables, up (towards callers), down (towards callees and tables) or both, from a node or a component: members per step with the edge wording, row and tier (fact or inferred with the weakest confidence), table edges with their access verification. Depth default 6, at most 10; bound caps, '? not modelled' ends and edges not followed are reported. An end is never 'unused'.

direction.description: up (callers, client calls, UI), down (callees, routes, handlers, tables) or both (default)

repository.description: project mode: the member (required when the project has several)

tools.title: Architecture chain

tools.description: What a changed item (or group) reaches: paths 'depends on' (fact) or 'may depend on' (inferred, confidence = weakest step), never 'breaks', depth default 3, at most 10; blind spots, near misses, gaps, table uses (a lower bound) and caps; in project mode across repositories through stored links, each with its assumption.

base.description: previous (default), run:ID, pin:NAME or a stored ref: base; project mode refuses ref: bases

A base that is not stored is refused; the server never indexes.

tools.name: impact
tools.title: Impact

tools.description: Project mode only: which cross-repository links changed between two kept link passes (the pass before the newest by default, or pass:N): links added, removed or changed with their kind and ends, paged. It reads the stored link journal only and never links or indexes; a single-repository server refuses it.

base.description: previous (default: the pass before the newest kept one) or pass:N, a kept link pass

limit.description: changed links per page (default 50, at most 500)

tools.name: link_changes
tools.title: Project link changes

tools.description: What the repository is made of: components (paged) with kinds, frameworks and counts, links by family with their weakest tier and cell states, databases, the schema summary and the precision summary (rules, labels, file counts). Unread components and unknown cells are unknowns.

repository.description: project mode: the member (required when the project has several)

scope.description: production (default) or all: which components the architecture view counts

unknowns_cursor.description: the next_cursor of an unknown's list

unknowns_limit.description: items of each list an unknown carries (call sites, sites, stubs; default 20, at most 500)

tools.name: overview
tools.title: Repository overview

tools.description: Show the current lines of a node, highlighted only when they are proven to be the indexed ones; any other state is shown with its reason.

context.description: lines around the span (default 8, at most 50)

repository.description: project mode: the member (required when the project has several)

target.description: node identity, 'METHOD /path' as served, a name or a qualified-name suffix at a name boundary

tools.name: source
tools.title: Source lines

tools.description: Is the index current, and what can be trusted? Freshness (changed files since the last index, paged), the last run, extractor match and precision refusal; in project mode every member and the link pass.

limit.description: changed files per page (default 50, at most 500)

tools.name: status
tools.title: Index status

tools.description: A table's schema (columns with their stored facts, claims by verification oracle or mapped, indexes, foreign keys, history, completeness, assumptions) and the code that reads, writes or builds a query on it with each use's verification and assumptions. Users are a lower bound (20 per page; include schema or users reads one half): sites that may also use the table are listed as unknowns, and a table whose access is not extracted says so; never 'no users'.

detail.description: compact (default: column facts with claim counts by verification) or full (every stored claim with its row and span)

include.description: both (default), schema (the table's facts only) or users (the code using it only)

repository.description: project mode: the member (required when the project has several)

scope.description: production (default) or all: which code users are listed

target.description: table identity, or a table's name or qualified-name suffix at a name boundary (tables only)

unknowns_cursor.description: the next_cursor of an unknown's list

unknowns_limit.description: items of each list an unknown carries (call sites, sites, stubs; default 20, at most 500)

tools.name: table
tools.title: Table schema and users

tools.description: What Graphvein could not link: the calls of a transport by status (dynamic, unmatched, ambiguous, ...) with their reasons, never links, and the endpoints with no stored caller in this scope, worded only so ('no stored caller', never 'dead').

repository.description: project mode: the member (required when the project has several)

status.description: comma-separated call statuses (default: every status but linked that the transport's summary counts)

tools.name: unresolved
tools.title: Unresolved calls and uncalled endpoints

assumptions.text: SQL runs against the schema source: The SQL text a modelled carrier runs, runs against the database the resolved schema source describes. sqlx query! checks this at compile time; for the other carriers it is an assumption, so their SQL edges are inferred.
Prisma receiver: A Prisma client receiver is what its name says.

labels.verification:mapped: mapped, not verified: the form is recognised by its documented meaning, no oracle ran it
labels.verification:oracle: verified by an oracle (the library or engine itself ran the form)

assumptions.text: Pins: The Prisma version in the package's lockfile is the one that creates the database.
Schema deployed: The database was created from this schema by Prisma Migrate or db push; hand-edited migration.sql is outside it.
Provider: The datasource URL points to a database of the declared provider.
Schema location: The schema found is the one the CLI uses (no --schema flag; the CLI runs in the package directory).
Default schema: The datasource URL has no schema parameter (or names public).
